page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6.large is a general-purpose virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 2 dedicated physical cores, 2 vCPUs, and 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 4.0 GB per core. This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage options. Network connectivity is defined by a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that the ecs.g6.large delivers modest performance across various workloads. In single-core evaluations, the instance achieves an average Geekbench score of 1163.0, placing it in the middle 50% of tested servers. However, multi-core performance is more constrained, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 1381.0 and a stress-ng multi-core CPU performance of 1735.44, both falling into the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth is also limited, registering 13.82 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 11.5 GB/sec for large block write operations.

Given its dedicated CPU allocation and balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the ecs.g6.large represents an entry-level general-purpose tier. It is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that require dedicated CPU resources but do not demand high computational throughput or massive memory bandwidth. Appropriate workloads include lightweight web serving, basic text processing, and small-scale development or testing environments. It is less suitable for database operations, software compilation, or high-throughput Redis deployments due to lower benchmark results in those areas.
